column1: # The restored sources the wasm32 port leaves out (owner decision, 2026-11-07: trim what the consumers do not
# need; give a trimmed part a simple implementation in Port/ when it turns out to be needed).
# pattern: a CMake regular expression matched against the source path relative to the repository root.
# reason: why the port leaves it out, and what replaces it, if anything.

column2: Swift has no Objective-C interoperation off Darwin; the units the port needs are rewritten in C or Objective-C under Port/Foundation
The cfprefsd client and its XPC sources; Port/CoreFoundation/OCFPortDefinitions.c keeps preferences in the process
XPC transport classes; no XPC in a browser
Markdown parsing (libcmark is unbound) and inflection
NSDecimal arithmetic is implemented in Swift; not reached by the consumers yet
NSDecimalNumber depends on the Swift NSDecimal arithmetic
The arm64 forwarding and invoking trampolines (naked assembly); Port/CoreFoundation/OCFForwardingPort.m forwards through objc4's wasm forward handler and keeps the type-string callbacks
NSScanner's decimal scanning parses with the Swift NSDecimal parser (Decimal is trimmed)
The empty bootstrap units assert the arm64 64-bit pointers, which wasm32 does not have
